# Sylentt: Full Context

> Sylentt Partners is Nic Aslett's fractional CIO practice: part-time IT and AI leadership for companies of about 20 to 150 employees.
> Based in Cache Valley, Utah. Works in person across Cache Valley and Northern Utah.

## About Sylentt

Sylentt Partners LLC trades as Sylentt. It is Nic Aslett's practice, and clients work with him directly. There is no team behind him, and that is the point: a client gets the person who has run IT departments for organizations their size, for a few hours a month, without a full-time salary.

The name comes from "silent partner": Nic works in the background so the client can run the business.

## Who it is for

Companies with roughly 20 to 150 employees, for example a manufacturer or a dental group, that have an IT company (a managed service provider, or MSP) for day-to-day support but no one steering IT.

What that usually looks like:

- **The IT company fixes things, but nobody decides things.** Projects stall, renewals auto-renew, and the roadmap lives in someone's head.
- **The company pays for software nobody uses and misses software it needs.** Nobody has the full list of what it pays for, who uses it, or when it renews.
- **Everyone says "use AI."** Nobody at the company owns figuring out where it actually helps and where it is a liability.
- **When the person who "knows the systems" leaves, so does the knowledge.** The passwords, the vendor contacts, and the reasons things are set up the way they are leave with them.

## How it works

### 1. IT & AI Assessment

Two weeks, one fixed price: $1,500. Nic inventories every system, subscription, vendor and risk; finds where AI fits and where it does not; and delivers a 12-month plan, presented in person.

Deliverables:

- Every system, subscription and vendor the client pays for, listed with its cost
- Contract and renewal dates in one place
- A security basics check
- Where AI can help, and where it is a risk
- A one-page AI policy for the team
- A 12-month plan
- A 1-hour walkthrough, in person

If the client continues on a monthly plan, the $1,500 comes off the first month. If the client does not continue, the plan is still theirs.

### 2. Retainer

Nic becomes the company's IT director for a set number of hours a month. He runs the roadmap, manages the IT company and other vendors, makes the decisions, and answers the questions.

- **Advisor: $1,500 a month, up to 8 hours.** A leadership meeting every month, management of the IT company and other vendors, the 12-month plan kept current, new software and AI tools checked before purchase, and email answers by the next business day.
- **Director: $2,500 a month, up to 16 hours.** Everything in Advisor, plus a check-in every week, ownership of the IT budget and renewals, and running one technology or AI project at a time.

### 3. The client owns everything

Documentation, roadmap, policies, vendor relationships: all the client's, in the client's accounts, from day one. Nothing lives in Nic's accounts, so ending the engagement needs no handover.

### Terms

- Prices are fixed and published at https://sylentt.com/pricing/.
- Month-to-month. 30 days' notice.
- Everything Nic produces belongs to the client.
- Hours cover meetings, email, and work done for the client.
- Extra hours are $150 each, only with the client's approval first.
- Unused hours do not carry over.

### What Nic does not do

- Helpdesk: the client's IT company keeps handling tickets.
- Hardware repair.
- After-hours support.
- Building software: when something needs to be built, Nic chooses who builds it and manages them.

## Frequently asked questions

**What does a fractional CIO actually do?**
The job a full-time IT director would do, for a few hours a month: making the technology decisions, planning the year, managing the IT company and other vendors, and owning the roadmap and the IT budget. Not the helpdesk. The IT company keeps fixing things; Nic makes sure the right things get fixed.

**We already have an IT company. Why would we need Nic?**
The IT company fixes things; Nic decides things. An IT company is paid to keep things running, not to decide where the company's technology should go. Nic manages it on the client's behalf and makes sure the client gets what it pays for.

**How is this different from an AI consultant?**
Nic is an IT leader who also handles AI. AI is evaluated like any other tool: where it saves money, where it creates risk, and what the rules are, delivered as a written policy the team can follow.

**How much of Nic's time does a client get?**
Advisor includes up to 8 hours a month and Director up to 16. Hours cover meetings, email, and work done for the client. If a month needs more, Nic asks first, and extra hours are $150 each. A month that needs less does not get invented work.

**What if it does not work out?**
Every plan is month-to-month with 30 days' notice. The client keeps everything produced: documentation, roadmap, policies, and vendor relationships, already in the client's accounts.

**Does Nic work outside Cache Valley?**
In person across Cache Valley and Northern Utah. Remote work elsewhere is the exception, not the rule.

## Experience

15+ years in IT, the last 10 leading teams of up to 40 people, including VP of IT at Fortidia, IT Manager at Charter Communications leading a 40-person QA team, and Release Train Engineer at Liqid. Nic has taken over IT departments that were not working and turned them around.

Past results from IT teams Nic has led (results, not a promise for any client):

- 100% on-time project delivery, as a rolling average, after he brought real project management to a 16-person IT department
- 80% faster ticket resolution: from 150 hours to 30
- SLA adherence doubled: from 40% to 80%

## Currently

Fractional CTO for edZOOcation (https://edzoocation.com/), a Shopify Plus education company. Nic designed and built their order-to-subscription automation, then handed the platform to their team and stepped into the leadership seat. About 8 hours a week of manual work was eliminated, and the team now runs its own systems.
